{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The printed entry's core is better supported by the cited texts and the sea/mountain framework than the common metonymy. Genesis 10:5 already treats isles as peoples marked off by tongue and nation; Isaiah 42:4 and 51:5 show those same isles waiting for and trusting God's law; Job 22:30 (unpointed iy) links the island to the delivered innocent; Isaiah 11:11 recovers a remnant from the islands; and Revelation 16:20 distinguishes islands that flee from mountains that are simply not found. Once sea = peoples and mountain = kingdom, an island as covenant ground standing out of that sea yields a set-apart people that waits for the law and is preserved when surrounding kingdoms fall. The common 'distant Gentile nations' reading captures the geographic reach but does not explain the waiting-for-law motif, the innocent-delivery motif, or the differential fate versus mountains. No material assertion printed in the entry is left unsupported.",
  "book_core_identification": "An island/isle is a set-apart (holy) people rising as covenant ground out of the sea of nations.",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "waiting for God's law",
    "preserved while surrounding kingdoms fall"
  ],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Chapter-only claim that islands disappear in the new creation solely because there is no longer a sea to be set apart from",
    "Chapter-only extension of the island figure through the full sea-of-glass / molten-sea typology",
    "Chapter-only identification of every personified sea or flood passage as strictly peoples-in-motion"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Island/isle is primarily a geographic or metonymic label for distant coastlands and remote Gentile nations (or the ends of the earth) that hear of, wait for, and receive God's salvation, without the further claim that they are covenant-ground peoples rising from and preserved out of a symbolic sea of nations.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Distant Gentile nations / remote coastlands of the earth.",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "SAME_CORE_BROADER",
  "material_core_denial": "The counter does not deny that the referent is peoples set apart from the mass; it simply stops at the broader geographic/ethnic label and refuses the covenant-ground / rising-from-sea mechanics.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Standard prophetic usage (Isa 41:1; 42:4; 49:1; 51:5; 60:9; Ps 97:1; Zeph 2:11) addresses isles as far-off nations that wait for Yahweh's law and glory.",
    "Genesis 10:5 already calls them 'isles of the Gentiles,' a Table-of-Nations geographic/ethnic division.",
    "Modern translations routinely render ʾiyyîm as 'coastlands,' treating the term as idiom rather than a freestanding symbol of holy remnant peoples.",
    "Revelation's fleeing islands can be read as ordinary cosmic-upheaval imagery without requiring a preserved-covenant-people contrast to mountains."
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Unifies Gen 10:5 (peoples marked off by tongue), Isa 42:4/51:5 (waiting for law = sanctification by truth), Job 22:30 (island of the innocent delivered), and Rev 16:20 (islands flee while mountains vanish) under one consistent figure.",
    "Derives the figure mechanically from already-established sea = peoples and mountain/rock = kingdom/covenant, so an island is simply covenant ground protruding from the sea.",
    "Explains the differential verb in Rev 16:20 (fled away vs. not found) as preservation of the set-apart versus dissolution of kingdoms.",
    "Accounts for the 'wait for his law' motif as the defining act of a people being set apart by the word."
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Stays closer to the surface geographic sense and to the majority of modern translational and commentary practice.",
    "Requires fewer interlocking symbol definitions (no need to presuppose the full sea/mountain system).",
    "Easily absorbs the missionary/universal-scope texts without additional typology."
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Genesis 10:5",
    "Isaiah 42:4",
    "Isaiah 51:5",
    "Job 22:30",
    "Isaiah 11:11",
    "Revelation 16:20",
    "Revelation 17:15 (sea = peoples) together with the mountain = kingdom premise"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [
    "Whether every occurrence of ʾiyyîm must carry the full set-apart-people sense, or whether some remain purely geographic.",
    "Whether the vowel-pointing issue in Job 22:30 is decisive or merely confirmatory."
  ],
  "confidence": "high"
}

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
